title: Properties of Materials
description: This course surveys materials, properties, and applications for technicians. Topics include a brief introduction to the properties of metals, polymers, ceramics, and composites.
outcomes: Compare properties of materials such as metals, polymers, ceramics, and composites.
Discuss the mechanical, electrical, thermal, and magnetic properties of common materials.
Identify evidence for corrosion, stress, wear, cracking, or other conditions that may lead to failure.
Briefly describe common materials and methods used in bioengineering, medical devices, semiconductors, nanotechnology, construction of buildings, roads, vessels, pipes, etc.
content: Properties and characteristics of major material types
Plastics, thermoplastics, thermosets, reinforced polymer composites
The effect of heat and cold on materials
Defects and failure; exploration of common causes of failures
assignments: Keep a laboratory notebook, showing experimental methods, results and data
Complete short essays which summarize important principles of materials science.
Example: "Discuss properties of stainless steel which make it superior to iron; list
Homework assignments that reinforce concepts from lectures, labs and reading.
notes: no objectives section in this format; units 1.5
